subject: Meridian POC: prompt/log batch acceptance, eval rubric & next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Alex Novak <alex@meridianhealth.ai>, Priya Singh <priya@meridianhealth.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Meridian POC: prompt/log batch acceptance, eval rubric & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks for the productive call earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we have a single source of truth before the handoff to engineering and data intake.

Agreed scope for the POC/trial:
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for Meridian’s triage & summarization assistant across 3 core workflows (clinical triage, referral summarization, patient messaging).
- Success criteria (high level):
  * Automated eval pass rate (accuracy/intent match) >= 78% across holdout test prompts
  * Human-rated helpfulness >= 4.0/5 on random sample (n=200)
  * Hallucination rate < 3% (as measured by our hallucination-check rubric)
  * Latency P95 <= 500ms on hosted trial config (we’ll confirm baseline SLA once we see sample distribution)

Deliverables Meridian to provide:
1) Prompt set: ~5k de-identified prompts covering the three workflows, annotated with workflow label and expected intent/expected answer when available. CSV preferred (see sample attached: meridian_prompt_sample.csv).
2) Server logs / raw query logs (redacted) for distribution & token-length profile (helpful but optional if logs unavailable).
3) Designated data owner & security contact for any PHI concerns.

Acceptance / eval plan (how Redwood will evaluate):
- Split: 80/10/10 train/validation/holdout (we only need the holdout for the POC evaluation; keep it sealed).
- Automated checks: format, deduplication, length distribution, and a light-label-consistency pass.
- Human eval: Redwood CS will run a human-rating batch (instructions attached) on a 200-sample random subset from the holdout to validate helpfulness and hallucination flags.
- Pass/Fail: POC considered successful if success criteria above met; if we miss by small margin we’ll propose an action plan (prompt augmentation, model variant).

Timeline (tentative):
- Apr 22: Meridian uploads initial prompt batch (minimum 1k) to S3 staging path.
- Apr 26: Redwood completes automated ingest + QA and returns ingest report + any required reformat asks.
- May 2: Human eval completed, initial results & follow-up call.

Ownership: Jordan Blake (technical ingestion & infra) will lead intake; Karthik Iyer will own eval metrics and human rating. Ben Carter is the commercial shepherd for the trial.

Upload guidelines & quick checklist are attached (s3-upload-instructions.pdf). If Meridian needs VPC/private deployment for PHI, flag that in your reply and we’ll coordinate the security checklist.

Please confirm the deliverables and the Apr 22 initial upload date. If that works, Alex / Priya — please share the S3 credentials or preferred secure transfer link and name your data owner.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: meridian_prompt_sample.csv (csv stub), s3-upload-instructions.pdf (pdf stub)

Subject: Re: Meridian POC: prompt/log batch acceptance, eval rubric & next steps

Thanks Neha — that recap matches our notes. A couple of clarifications from our side: 
- We will provide an initial batch of ~1.2k prompts by Apr 22 (good to start with that minimum). We will aim for the full ~5k by Apr 30.
- Because the data is healthcare-adjacent we need to run the trial in a Private deployment (VPC) — we discussed that briefly on the call. Security team is already engaged and will need the SOC2 evidence & network checklist.
- I’ll have Priya (copied) be the data owner for transfer; she’ll share the staging S3 bucket and a short inventory CSV.

S3 staging info (temporary): https://s3-us-east-1.amazonaws.com/meridian-staging/ready-for-ingest/
We’ll send IAM creds to Jordan via the secure link you provide.

We also want the eval to include a short custom metric: "safety_flags_per_1000" (count of outputs with safety-related flags per 1000 responses) — if Redwood can compute that from the human rating rubric, great.

Alex Novak
Head of Product, Meridian Health
alex@meridianhealth.ai

Subject: Re: Meridian POC: prompt/log batch acceptance, eval rubric & next steps

Alex — perfect, thanks for the quick confirmation and for naming Priya as the data owner. A few follow-ups/action items from Redwood: 
1) Private deployment: noted. I’ve looped in Jordan (cc) to scope the VPC steps and security checklist. We’ll push SOC2 artifacts and the questionnaire to the secure drive link by EOD.
2) Safety metric: we can compute safety_flags_per_1000 from the human rating pass/fail flags; Karthik will include that in the evaluation report.
3) Upload path & naming convention — please put uploads as: /meridian/poctrial/YYYYMMDD_<batch-name>.csv. Include a small manifest.csv with column mapping (prompt_text, workflow_label, expected_answer (optional), id).

Minimum format requirements (short):
- UTF-8 CSV, header row mandatory
- prompt_text (string), workflow_label (one of: triage, referral, messaging), id (unique), expected_answer (optional), redaction_flag (yes/no)

Jordan — once you have S3 creds from Alex/Priya, can you confirm whether we need a presigned upload or if you prefer us to pick up from their bucket? We can support both (we can run the ingest from our side into the Private trial environment).

Next steps summary:
- Apr 22: Meridian uploads first batch (1k+).
- Apr 23: Jordan confirms creds & ingestion method.
- Apr 26: Redwood returns ingest report and any reformat asks.

Neha
